main_statement_findings.finding: The literal greedy spanner and its real edge count are bounded by2*fullDensityLoss(h)*h^(2/(r+1))*n. The density witness is internally constructed, and its independent degree-nine logarithmic upper bound has constants independent of r. The endpoint covers finite simple graphs and positive r,h; its published weight hypothesis remains global Sym2 positivity.

The explicit ErdosGirthConjecture is the standard fixed-r positive-constant/eventual-size premise. The output quantifiers give one positive constant for fixed r, every h>=3 and every sufficiently large exact n. Real graphs, minor exclusion, high girth and every-spanner lower bounds are constructed. The connected completion supplies an actual original MST and lightness lower bound, so no disconnected-MST inference remains.

The positive-edge theorem constructs a spanner and an original input MST, retaining the true weight ratio. There is no supplied phase, payment, hierarchy, covering stream, cutoff or selected initial-state premise. Its explicit bound has exactly the claimed h exponent and polylog h, and the sufficiently-small-epsilon cubic/logarithmic dependence.

For0<epsilon<=1/2, delta=epsilon and log_2(1/epsilon)>=1, so log_2(8097/epsilon)+1 <= (log_2(8097)+2)*log_2(1/epsilon). For h>=3, Nat.log_2(h)+2 is O(log h). Thus the explicit universal inequality implies the stated asymptotic form. This review establishes the mathematical correspondence; the published theorem is quantitative rather than a Lean IsBigO declaration.

The original main novel theorems are existential sparsity/lightness bounds and conditional lower bounds. No executable complexity theorem is asserted there. Historical README runtime placeholders do not create a missing source theorem; no executable-runtime certification should be claimed.

corrections_preserved: Printed Claim19 overstates the guaranteed weighted girth. The development uses stretch+1 throughout, and the canonical numerical scale bridges that corrected threshold into the final proof.

The lower-bound h>=3 restriction is necessary: a K2-minor-free graph has no edges, so a positive linear lower bound at h=2 is false. This is a correction to the unqualified wording, not an unproved construction premise.
The introductory lightness-versus-sparsity assertion is not needed by the corrected connected lower witness; its earlier documented counterexample remains separate.
remaining_qualifications: Exact478 remote CI is still pending; full452 does not certify the478 successor.

Published478 lightness assumes connected input with n>=2 and h>=3. On nontrivial connected positive-h inputs h>=3 is automatic, but that reduction and the singleton/zero-MST convention are only later unpublished drafts at review time. Count those only after their exact review/gates/binding.
Published478 sparsity assumes globally positive Sym2 weights. The edge-only extension follows using the reviewed transport interface, but its final wrapper is later unpublished at review time.

Disconnected inputs with a spanning-forest convention and zero/negative actual-edge weights are not covered by these endpoints. The paper defines lightness through an MST, so this audit accepts the conventional connected positive-weight model only; do not silently market it as a formalized forest or zero-weight extension.

This is an independent main-statement/endpoint/dependency-scope audit combined with the prior exact component reviews, not a second line-by-line audit of all478 proof modules or cited background theorems. Conjecture8 and the cited Erdos conjecture are not claimed proved.
